reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess target engagement for either pembrolizumab (PD-1) or talimogene laherparepvec (TNFRSF14). PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarker data reported to assess downstream biology changes from either checkpoint blockade or oncolytic viral mechanisms. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (PFS) failed in both arms - combination arm achieved 14.3 months vs 8.5 months for placebo+pembrolizumab control (p=0.13, not significant). OS also failed (p=0.77). The combination showed numerical improvement over control but did not reach statistical significance. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Trial appears adequately powered (n=713) with appropriate duration (median follow-up 25-36 months). Safety profile was manageable with similar rates between arms. This appears to be a straightforward efficacy failure rather than a design issue.

failure_modes.evidence: No biomarker or target engagement data available to determine where in the causal chain the failure occurred. Cannot assess whether pembrolizumab engaged PD-1 or whether talimogene laherparepvec engaged TNFRSF14 or activated oncolytic pathways.
